summary: Toast: Provider + Viewport, everything else through useToast() — the per-toast anatomy is deliberately not public API, because all twelve measured call sites hand data to a manager. Built on Base UI Toast: queue, timers, stack measurement, swipe and announcement come from there; the surface is the Popover panel's recipe on radius-lg with shadow-lg, one size, at --ui-dialog-width-md. Five types (info/success/warning/danger/loading) carried ONLY by a leading intent glyph — the fill never tints, so a stack does not read as a traffic light; Base UI's promise() stamps `error` and the renderer treats it as danger, keeping the library's vocabulary (CONVENTIONS §2). Four things came out of building it. (1) The title is text-body-lg, not text-title-sm: the title roles are fluid and a toast is a fixed-width surface, so title-sm would compute below the sheet's 16px — the browser test asserts the computed 16. (2) The split transition (transforms on the spring pair, opacity on duration-slow, height on duration-fast) cannot be one Tailwind shorthand, so it ships as longhand arbitrary properties — and check:utilities' transition rules could not see those, demanding a shorthand the component avoids: the gate now parses [transition-property:…] and its class extractor admits arbitrary-property classes at all (they were filtered before any rule ran). Probed failing-first through the new path, both rules. (3) Four contrast pairs joined NONTEXT_CONTRAST_PAIRS — each intent fg on bg-elevated, a ground no intent ink had ever been measured against (5.38–5.62:1 light, 7.23–8.56:1 dark). (4) The geometry harness accepts "|"-separated child slots, because the content row is four different parts in one track and the union-gap laws want all of them; toast contributes three geometry cases (shell → content row → text column) split across Root and Content where Paper draws one padded node — the deviation is recorded in the spec. The viewport's landmark label and the close button's accessible name are REQUIRED props; axe caught duplicate landmarks in the stories the first time two viewports shared a name.
